No. The evidence shows tree-cover loss on only a small part of the property in 2021, not the whole of it.

- Hansen/UMD mapped about 81.3 ha of tree-cover loss in 2021. That is roughly 2.2% of the 3,643.5 ha property.
- A further 37.3 ha was lost in patches under 0.5 ha. These are not counted as an event.
- The loss is corroborated. A later year was observed, and the JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area.
- The forest map for the loss area shows mostly planted forest (68.1 ha of pine, *Pinus elliottii* and *Pinus taeda*). The rest (13.2 ha) lies outside mapped forest, and none is native forest.

This evidence does not establish deforestation or land-use change, because Hansen loss also includes cutting a plantation. It also does not establish the cause, legality, who was responsible, or any compliance finding.
